The core problem: You have Ammachi's real photos from age ~60-80s, and you need to generate her at age ~20-30 (1940s-50s era) for the video's middle sections.

Based on the research from earlier, here is the complete guide for de-aging to age 12-15:
The core challenge: Going to age 12-15 is harder than going to 25 because you need to reverse puberty changes — rounder face, softer jaw, no defined cheekbones, bigger eyes relative to face, smoother forehead, fuller cheeks. The young adult photo is your best anchor.
Best approach — use BOTH photos together:
The young photo (age 20-30) gives you the bone structure and features before aging. The old photo (age 50-70) confirms what features are consistently theirs across time. Together they help the AI understand what is permanent versus what changed with age.
Prompt template:
"Create a photorealistic portrait of this same person as they would have looked at age 13. Use the younger photo as the primary face reference. Maintain identical nose shape, eye shape, ear shape and bone structure. Make the face rounder and fuller with softer jawline. Bigger eyes relative to face. Fuller cheeks. Smooth forehead. No facial hair. Hair natural and simple. Same skin tone. 1930s Kerala, natural light."
Key things to specify for age 12-15:

Rounder softer face — jaw not yet defined

Fuller cheeks — baby fat still present

Eyes appear larger relative to face size

Shorter neck

Smaller overall head relative to body

For girls — center-parted oiled hair in two plaits or loose bun

For boys — simply combed oiled hair
Reference images — how to use them:
Upload both photos in the same message and say clearly:

Young photo → "primary face reference — take bone structure from here"

Old photo → "secondary confirmation of features only"
Most important instruction: The biggest mistake is asking for too much change at once. Do it in two steps:
Step 1:
"Make this person look 18 years old"
Step 2 — in same chat:
"Now make them look 13 years old — rounder face, fuller cheeks, softer jaw"
Two steps always gives better results than jumping straight to age 13 from an adult photo.

The fundamental tension: identity preservation versus age control

Every AI age progression method wrestles with the same tradeoff. Stronger face-identity locking (higher IP-Adapter weight, more ControlNet influence) fights against the age-transformation prompt, producing a "copy-paste" effect where the reference photo's age bleeds through. Weaker identity locking allows age changes but risks losing the person's likeness entirely. The sweet spot for most tools is an identity weight of 0.7–0.85, low enough to let age descriptors take effect while high enough to preserve distinctive facial features.

This tension is especially acute when de-aging — generating a childhood photo from an elderly reference. The structural changes between a 10-year-old's face and a 95-year-old's face are enormous: rounder skull proportions, larger eye-to-face ratio, smoother skin, undeveloped bone structure. Going older from a young reference is far more predictable, since AI models have abundant training data showing aging patterns. Going younger requires the model to "imagine" bone structure in reverse, which every method handles less reliably.

For your project, this means: start from your youngest anchor photo (age ~25) and work backward for childhood, and work forward from each anchor for intermediate ages. Use the age-65 and age-72 photos as validation checkpoints — if the AI-generated age-60 and age-70 images don't resemble those anchors, adjust your approach before continuing.
